limits: The plan's write scopes come from a committed snapshot of its backlog. The plan folder is in no repository, so CI checks the snapshot's shape and that the map is derived from it; only snapshot-plan.mjs --check, run on a machine that has the backlog, can refute the snapshot itself.
The list of reserved paths is a recorded input from the coordinator's pre-push checklist, which is also in no repository. A changed checklist needs a new rules file and a regenerated map.

Ownership is judged on repository-relative path names only. File contents, symlinks and file modes are not examined, and a rename in a git diff is listed as a delete and an add so both names are checked.
Whether a reserved path exists in becoder or beval is judged against the required artifacts of the baseline lock; no other file of those repositories is visible to this check.
The nested test runner is a bskel file, so suites are compared with the map for bskel only. The scopes of the becoder and beval tracks come from the plan alone.
A path inside no track scope fails as unowned. Stable surface files are not free for any track; they need a change of the map.

The map is derived from the live SUITES list and from the files named test/t00-*.test.mjs. When either changes, the map must be regenerated with build-ownership-map.mjs and committed, or the check fails.
Owning a scope is not support or completion: a track that owns a path has not thereby delivered anything in it.
